thread_b.role: concurrent XFRM policy lookup updating lifetime (writer)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([write(use_time)]) (a store to the shared timestamp must be single-copy, not torn by a concurrent store to the same field)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@xfrm_lookup_with_ifid:3223 = WRITE(use_time = ktime_get_real_seconds()) by the other worker on the SAME shared xfrm_policy
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: neither worker holds any lock for this field; both reach the same shared policy via lookup and store concurrently -> no serialize, no order
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent conflicting write-write -> data race; explicitly intentionally-racy/benign (both write the same monotonically-advancing timestamp)

fix_maps_to: patch wraps the store in WRITE_ONCE -> single-copy atomicity for the store; NO exclusion/order added (the concurrent stores remain, just marked) -> maps to making atomic([write]) hold at the access-marking level only
recall_risk_notes: Benign write-write race the author explicitly calls 'intentionally racy'; required_ordering = 'must be marked as single-copy stores' (no exclusion/order needed). This is exactly the finding our design wants to AVOID degenerating into (pure syntactic race detector, §10), so the arbiter would likely reject the atomic(write) assume -> FN. Also a self-race on a SHARED (mis-assumed-private) policy: static must (a) realize the policy is shared across two xfrm_lookup_with_ifid instances and (b) model the same entry on two CPUs.
